🔥 Koitalel’s Last Walk — The Betrayal That Changed Kenya

On the morning of 19 October 1905, the Nandi hills were silent.
Too silent.
Even the wind felt like it was holding its breath.

Koitalel arap Samoei — the Orkoiyot, the prophet, the defender of the Nandi — stood outside his hut, watching the sun rise slowly over the valleys he had protected for more than ten years.

His warriors circled around him.
They begged him not to go.
The British had requested a “peace meeting,” but something felt wrong… painfully wrong.

Koitalel looked at his people and said quietly,
“If I fear death, then I have no right to lead you.”

And so he walked.
Down the familiar paths.
Past the river where he once played as a child.
Toward the forest clearing where history waited with a loaded gun.

When he arrived, he found the British officer, Colonel Meinertzhagen, smiling.
A fake smile.
Behind the trees, a hidden rifleman waited.
Koitalel didn’t know — or maybe he knew, and still chose courage over fear.

As he stepped forward to greet the officer, a shot cracked through the air.
One shot.
The shot that ended a decade of resistance…
and broke the heart of a nation.

Koitalel fell, but the forest didn’t stay silent.
The wind rose.
The birds scattered.
And every Nandi elder swore that the earth itself shook in anger.

To his people, Koitalel did not die that day.
He simply crossed into the world of the ancestors…
to continue watching over the land he fought for.

Maksud Kafir dalam Islam

Dalam bahasa Arab, kāfir (كَافِر) berasal daripada perkataan kafara, yang bermaksud menutup atau menyembunyikan.

Dalam konteks Islam, istilah kafir digunakan untuk merujuk kepada:

Seseorang yang tidak beriman kepada Allah dan ajaran Islam

Iaitu orang yang menolak, tidak percaya, atau menutup hati daripada menerima kebenaran ajaran islam.

Istilah umum bagi sesiapa yang tidak beriman kepada Allah, Rasul, dan ajaran Islam — sama ada dia menolak, meragu, atau tidak mahu menerima Islam.

⸻

Jenis-jenis Kafir (Mengikut ulama)

Ulama membahagikan “kafir” kepada beberapa kategori berdasarkan sikap atau tindakan:
1. Kafir Harbi
Orang yang memerangi umat Islam.

2. Kafir Zimmi
Orang bukan Islam yang tinggal dalam negara Islam dan dilindungi.

3. Kafir Musta’min
Bukan Islam yang masuk sementara ke negara Islam (pelancong, peniaga) dengan jaminan keselamatan.

4. Kafir Mu’ahid
Bukan Islam yang ada perjanjian damai dengan umat Islam.

5. Kafir Kitabi
Penganut agama Samawi seperti Kristian dan Yahudi (Ahli Kitab).

⸻

Penting untuk difahami

> Perkataan “kafir” bukan penghinaan, tetapi istilah teologi (agama).
- Ia merujuk kepada status akidah, bukan menghakimi karakter seseorang.
- Islam tetap memerintahkan untuk berbuat baik, berlaku adil dan menghormati orang bukan Islam.

Contoh ayat arahan dalam Al-Quran:

“Allah tidak melarang kamu berbuat baik dan berlaku adil kepada orang-orang yang tidak memerangi kamu…”
— Surah Al-Mumtahanah: 8

“Dalam Islam, istilah ‘kafir’ bukan penghinaan. Ia hanya istilah agama yang bermaksud seseorang yang belum menerima ajaran Islam. Sama seperti istilah ‘non-Muslim’. Islam tetap ajar kita hormat, berlaku adil dan berbuat baik kepada semua.”

🌱 Wrapping Up Phase II: Supporting the Mental Health of Children in De-Occupied Regions of Ukraine 🇺🇦💛💙

Over the past two years, our collaboration with NGO Community Self-Help (CSH) has strengthened the ability of frontline workers to recognize and respond to the mental health needs of children and families living through the impacts of war.

In Phase I, we built the foundation by training 100+ frontline workers across 5 regions in basic MHPSS principles. These sessions not only developed skills—they also helped reduce isolation among responders and highlighted the need for further, locally tailored training.

Phase II advanced this work by adapting the Global MHPSS curriculum for Ukraine and launching a Training of Trainers (ТoT) pathway. Through two 5-day trainings and four ToTs, we reached 112 workers from 28 institutions and supported the first graduate-led trainings in two cities close to the frontline, reaching 30 additional responders.

A new network of local trainers, guided by Ukrainian psychologists and supported remotely by CSH, is now helping shape a more sustainable, locally led training model.

We’re excited to carry this momentum forward as we move into Phase III, continuing to build a strong, resilient system of MHPSS training in Ukraine. 🇺🇦✨
